alignments.note: The ASV renders the single verb by the periphrasis 'she lifted up her voice', the supplied subject and possessive riding along as rule 7 helpers. Head corrected from 'lifted' to 'voice': rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it is finite or the phrase's formal head, and 'voice' is what answers to the φων- root of ἀναφωνέω while 'lifted up' carries only the ἀνα- and the frame. This is the reading the chapter takes elsewhere for a cognate periphrasis — μακαριοῦσίν → 'shall call ... blessed' heads on 'blessed' at 1:48 and ἐκραταιοῦτο → 'waxed strong' on 'strong' at 1:80. Heading on 'lifted' remains defensible if 'lifted up' is read as carrying content of its own rather than as the frame.
Anarthrous dative noun; the case preposition 'with' and the supplied 'a' both ride with it (rules 21 and 51's anarthrous clause), discontinuously across the adjective under rule 15.
Verbless clause with a participial predicate: the predicate carries the supplied copula (rule 53), headed on 'Blessed'.
The predicate carries the supplied copula and the subject is a noun phrase, so rules 53 and 63 keep '*is*' here rather than on ὁ καρπός.
The determiner slot of 'womb' is occupied by the possessive realizing σου, so the article realizes nothing (rule 20).
Genitive noun with its case preposition; rule 21 leaves 'of' on the noun where no article carries a determiner, and rule 15 permits the discontinuity across 'thy'.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive 'thy' (rule 20).
